patch.value: Mirror the published refusal projection for whitespace-adjacent credential layouts

The native refusal-projection URL scanner (src/refusal.rs userinfos) and the published CLI token-wise redaction (dist/core/shared/url-credentials.js redactUrlCredentialsInText) disagree on three whitespace-adjacent layouts, verified against the pinned 2026.11.18 oracle: (1) a space in the user part with an encoded separator ('user :pass%40evil.com') - the oracle masks the password token while native keeps it, because the percent-encoded fallback splits the authority at whitespace and keeps only the first segment; (2) a scheme-less credential in prose with an encoded separator ('host.invalid/path user:pass%40evil.com') - the oracle masks while native scans only from URL schemes; (3) a space inside the password with a literal separator ('user:pa ss@evil.com') - the oracle keeps the text unchanged while native masks up to the @. A fix must keep every corpus case in tests/support/refusal_corpus.rs and the differential refusal suites byte-identical.
Compare the native and published redaction for each whitespace-adjacent layout and close every divergence with corpus and differential coverage.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Reproduced all three recorded divergences using synthetic stored blocker titles and the full start-task refusal. The exact Round GP input with whitespace in the password before %40 produced identical refusal bytes. Both also kept the public URL followed by an email. The existing literal-at redaction protects stored text in native output, so coordinate that difference with the published CLI before choosing a parity change.
